412.t: Pee Wee Russell and the start of Pee Wee and Art's Back Room
412.s: Hodes tells how he and Pee Wee Russell, both broke, walked to find a job in 1949. The union let them run the club for six months before the delegation spoke.
412.q: And so I was at one place six months before the delegation came up and said to me, we know you're there, we've been knowing you're there. You haven't come up and told us, but we know you're there. We figured to give you a chance to get this thing started. And that was Pee Wee (and Art's) Back Room.…

412.t: Back in New York: still working at trad places
412.s: Hodes says the trouble did not run him out of town. He worked at Ryan's and the Vanguard, and Nick and Condon gave him some jobs.
412.ch: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
412.q: Well, I'm back to New York. All this is a New York happening. There's an involvement, there's a life there, it's alive. Even getting into all this trouble was an alive thing. It did not run me out of the business, didn't run me out of town. I was still able to find some --

256.t: Jimmy Ryan's and the move to Condon's
256.s: After the Mills Cavalcade he plays Jimmy Ryan's, then is hired at the Greenwich Village Condon's over Pesky's objections.
256.q: And then I still went back. I was down at Nick's. In and out, in and out, in and out. So, uh, then I leave there. After I leave the Mills Cavalcade, uh, I went to Jimmy Ryan's for five and a half months. Did a terrific job there, thank God. And then, uh, I went down to Connors, and Connors was a…

224.t: Slugs with Joe Henderson, Chick Corea; Sonny Rollins at the Audubon
224.s: He led bands with Joe Henderson and Chick Corea at Slugs, and one with Sonny Rollins and Kenny Dorham at the Audubon.
224.q: I had Joe down at Slugs with me. In fact, I got some – somewhere around here I got some reel-to-reel of a little of that, if one of my slick sons didn’t take it and do something with it. I was looking for that. I had some people interviewing me. I was looking for it. I couldn’t find it then. I got…

400.t: Joe Glaser books Taylor's trio; the Hickory House and Basin Street West in 1954
400.s: Taylor explains how Glaser's office got his trio a tour from the Hickory House, and they recall the downstairs Basin Street West on 51st Street.
400.ch: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
400.q: Yeah 51st Street, downstairs. That was Basin Street West, yeah I was there.

80.t: How he came to play the Embers, following Louis Metcalf and Jonah Jones
80.s: He played the Embers in the 1960s, following Metcalf and Jonah Jones, in and out with a changing group.
80.q: Yes. Yes. Louie Metcalf was one of the first guys I knew to have gone there, and stayed there for a while, in and out. He and Jonah Jones.

67.t: Eddie Heywood's sextet at Cafe Society
67.s: He stayed with Eddie Heywood Jr.'s sextet at Cafe Society, a long-lasting job all in New York, until 1945.
67.ch: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
67.q: We didn't go anywhere with that band.

9.t: Leonard Feather and wealthy Bobby Burnet form a small group
9.s: At the Rhythm Club Feather asked him to join a mixed combination with trumpeter Bobby Burnet, a young millionaire who dressed like a tramp.
9.ch: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
9.q: I was talking about how I was at the Rhythm Club one day, my favorite hangout spot where the musicians gathered to get the gigs and one thing and another, and Leonard Feather walked up to me and asked me would I be interested in working in a small combination with Bobby Burnet, a trumpet player. I…

231.t: A little Broadway revue on 46th Street between films
231.s: Between 1947 and 1961 he played a small club on 46th Street with a five-piece band and dancer Mae Barnes; it lasted about three weeks.
231.ch: Solo years, marriages and the Canadian party
231.q: '47 and '61. Yeah, I was in New York. I performed at this club on Broadway, this was 46th Street and Broadway, a little club, a combination, a little revue, about four people and a band, 5-piece band.

18.t: Boston and New York in the early 1950s
18.s: He led two bands in Boston with Rex Stewart in the first, then opened Wally's in New York.
18.q: I worked in the Savoy and I worked in the High-Hat. I had Rex Stewart in my band out there.

72.s: Moore clarifies which Ryan's he means and mentions five years there with Tony Parenti after the war.
72.q: But see, the Jimmy Ryan's on 52nd Street was down further. It's on the East Side. See, we was on the West Side.

75.s: He led groups with Rudy Rutherford and Ronnie Coles at the Shalimar uptown and played Minton's.
75.ch: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
75.q: Oh boy, that's another one. We can't forget the Shalimar! Oh, on and off, about a month at a time. I had a group there with Rudy Rutherford, Ronnie Coles and (?) Richardson.

76.t: Long residencies at the Vanguard and Ryan's
76.s: Berg's picked up Zutty's option for a year; Dance and Marge praise long residencies, and Zutty tells how he opened Ryan's and changed the Vanguard's clientele, bringing the band to Ryan's after Milt Gabler's sessions.
76.q: And Zutty could have stayed in Jimmy Ryan's as long as he wanted to stay. Because they always, Zutty opened the store. The very first band that went in Jimmy Ryan's.

86.t: Continuing his group after Joe Williams: quartet in New York
86.s: He kept Forrest with new pianists and drummers, then worked quartet jobs at the Arpeggio Room, Embers and Roundtable.
86.ch: Jazz at the Philharmonic and later years
86.q: Joe? I continued on with the group. I got Hugh Lawson . He played piano with me. And had the same group. Not Elvin, but I had Clarence -- he was a drummer, used to be with Dizzy. Clarence Johnson.

103.t: The Embers: Jo Jones trio with Tyree Glenn and Hank Jones
103.s: They sort out the Embers jobs with Joe Bushkin, Tommy Potter and Hank Jones, and how his trio became Tyree Glenn's quartet for 17 and 16 weeks.
103.q: You know you went up and down the Street for one year, one block one year. I did a little house there with Dorothy Donegan and Joe Bushkin and Tyree Glenn. Of course, I had the trio there with Hank Jones, my original trio with Hank Jones, Tommy Potter -

79.t: Trio at the Vanguard, then Barney Bigard's group
79.s: He took a trio into the Vanguard for several months, twice. After Wilson, Barney Bigard offered Thomas a job at Fat Man's on 155th Street, and arranged around his own college dates. He calls it a terrific group.
79.ch: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
79.q: I don't know but we had a nice little deal down there for maybe three or four months and we came on back and did three or four months again.
